about: Exercise library for Long Life Lifts rotation (the athlete, Oct 24, 2026: the coach proposes exercise swaps when a training block starts; the athlete accepts or keeps). One row per exercise with a stable id: every logged set is stored under this id (coach/strength_log.csv exercise_id), so an exercise that leaves the routine and comes back later keeps its whole history. pattern = the movement slot it can fill (a swap keeps the pattern, dose and time); favors = what it carries over to (bike, run, trail = climbing and descending, swim, health); why = one line for the proposal; the dose fields (sets, lo, hi, unit, load, per_side, step, next_hard, extra, legs) are copied into coach/strength.json when the exercise is swapped in. Equipment is what the athlete has at home: dumbbells, kettlebells, bench, pull-up bar, bands, a box or step. cautions name the stop signals that matter for it. needs = the equipment it takes (dumbbells also means kettlebells; an empty list is bodyweight only), read by lifts.py library and lifts.py start when a new coach builds its first routine. norm: powerlifting with norm_key (the barbell back squat, bench press and deadlift, 6.88.0) means a person who does that lift has its key lift tile ranked against powerlifters of their sex and age (coach/norms.json, van den Hoek 2024); every other lift shows the person's own progress (the athlete, Nov 15, 2026). the athlete themselves does no barbell deadlifts (CURRENT-STATE: elbow and back history).

rows.name: Pistol squat
rows.why: Single-leg strength, balance and ankle control in one move; a warm-up that loads the stance leg.
rows.next_hard: box → floor → balance platform, then hold a DB
rows.how: Stand on one leg in front of a box or bench; sit back slowly until you touch it; drive up through the whole foot, knee over toes

rows.name: Slow step-down (4 s down)
rows.why: Slow lowering off a step trains the quads and knee control for long descents (eccentric load).
rows.cautions: knee pain at the front of the knee: lower step
rows.how: Stand on a step on one leg; lower the other heel slowly to touch the floor; keep the knee tracking over the middle toes

rows.name: Single-leg pogo hops
rows.why: Short, stiff ankle hops build the spring that running economy depends on.
rows.how: Small quiet hops on one foot; land soft on the forefoot, knee slightly bent; stop if the ankle or Achilles complains

rows.name: 2 s pause front squat
rows.why: Upright, quad-led squat with a pause at the bottom: the knee and hip angles and the push of the bike's power stroke.
rows.how: Bar on the front of the shoulders, elbows high; sit down between the heels; hold 2 s at the bottom, then stand tall

rows.name: DB walking lunge
rows.why: One leg at a time in a moving stance: hip and knee stability and glute work close to running and hiking.
rows.cautions: ankle above a twinge: switch to reverse lunges in place
rows.how: Long step forward; lower the back knee near the floor; push through the front heel into the next step

rows.name: Rear-foot-elevated split squat
rows.why: The heaviest single-leg squat you can load with dumbbells: quads and glutes for climbing, without a heavy bar.
rows.how: Back foot on a bench, front foot a stride ahead; drop the back knee straight down; drive up through the front heel

rows.name: Goblet squat
rows.why: The simplest loaded squat; a light-week or restart option.
rows.how: Hold one dumbbell at the chest, elbows down; sit between the heels with the chest up; stand by pushing the floor away

rows.name: Weighted pull-up
rows.why: Vertical pull for the swim catch and posture.
rows.how: Hang with straight arms, hands just past shoulder width; pull the chest to the bar; lower all the way under control

rows.name: One-arm DB row
rows.why: Horizontal pull with an anti-rotation hold; easier on the elbow than pull-ups.
rows.cautions: the option when the elbow aches on pull-ups
rows.how: One hand and knee on the bench, back flat; pull the dumbbell to the hip; lower slowly to a full stretch

rows.name: DB Romanian deadlift
rows.why: Both-leg hinge: hamstrings, glutes and back strength with a load you can progress.
rows.how: Dumbbells at the thighs, soft knees; push the hips back with a flat back until the hamstrings stretch; squeeze the glutes to stand

rows.name: Single-leg DB Romanian deadlift
rows.why: One-leg hinge: hip stability and glute control in the stance that running asks for; heavy enough with home dumbbells.
rows.how: Stand on one leg, soft knee; hinge forward as the free leg reaches back; keep the hips level, then stand tall

rows.name: Single-leg hip thrust (back on bench)
rows.why: Direct glute work at full hip extension; low back load.
rows.how: Upper back on a bench, one foot planted; drive the hips up until the body is straight; pause and lower slowly

rows.name: Incline DB bench
rows.why: Upper-body push for balance with the pulls.
rows.how: Bench at about 30 degrees; lower the dumbbells to the sides of the chest; press up and slightly in

rows.name: Push-up (feet raised when easy)
rows.why: Push with a moving shoulder blade; no bench needed.
rows.next_hard: feet on the bench, then a backpack
rows.how: Hands under the shoulders, body in one line; lower the chest to a fist above the floor; press back up without sagging

rows.name: Band face pulls
rows.why: Rear shoulder and upper back for posture on the bike and in the water.
rows.how: Band at face height; pull toward the eyes, hands apart, elbows high; squeeze the shoulder blades and return slowly

rows.name: Band Y-T-W
rows.why: Lower trap and rotator cuff for the overhead swim stroke.
rows.how: Light band, arms long; raise into a Y, then a T, then pull to a W; keep the ribs down and move slowly

rows.name: Chest-down rear delt fly
rows.why: Rear shoulder and upper back with light dumbbells, chest on an incline bench: the band face pull's job without a band.
rows.how: Chest down on an incline bench; raise light dumbbells out to the sides with a slight elbow bend; lower slowly

rows.name: Split squat
rows.why: One leg at a time with no kit: quads and glutes in a running stance.
rows.next_hard: back foot on a chair, then hold a bag
rows.how: Feet a stride apart, back heel up; lower the back knee straight down; stand by pushing through the front foot

rows.name: Band squat
rows.why: A loaded squat that packs in a bag: stand on the band, handles at the shoulders.
rows.how: Stand on the band, ends at the shoulders; squat down with the chest up; stand fully against the band

rows.name: Kettlebell deadlift
rows.why: The hinge learned with one bell between the feet; the step before the swing.
rows.how: Kettlebell between the feet; hinge the hips back with a flat back and grip it; stand tall by driving the hips forward

rows.name: Kettlebell swing
rows.why: A fast hip snap: power and the back of the legs in a few minutes.
rows.cautions: lower back takes the swing instead of the hips: back to deadlifts
rows.how: Hike the bell back between the legs; snap the hips forward so it floats to chest height; let it fall and hinge again

rows.name: Single-leg glute bridge
rows.why: Glutes at full hip extension with nothing but the floor.
rows.next_hard: shoulders on a couch, then a pause at the top
rows.how: Lie on your back, one foot planted near the hip; lift the hips until straight; pause and lower slowly

rows.name: Band Romanian deadlift
rows.why: The hinge with a band under the feet: hamstrings and glutes on the road.
rows.how: Stand on the band, ends in hand; push the hips back with a flat back; stand by squeezing the glutes

rows.name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
rows.why: The heavy hinge from the top down: hamstrings and back with a load you can keep adding to.
rows.cautions: lower back feels uneven or rounds: stop
rows.how: Bar at the thighs, soft knees; slide it down the legs as the hips go back; stand when the hamstrings stretch, back flat

rows.name: Table row
rows.why: Lie under a sturdy table and pull your chest to the edge: the home pull with no kit.
rows.next_hard: walk the feet further out, then raise them
rows.how: Lie under a sturdy table and grip its edge; pull the chest up with the body straight; lower slowly

rows.name: Band row
rows.why: A seated or standing row on a band anchored at chest height.
rows.how: Band anchored at chest height; pull the hands to the ribs, elbows close; squeeze the shoulder blades and return slowly

rows.name: Pull-up
rows.why: The bodyweight vertical pull; a band or a slow lowering when full reps are not there yet.
rows.how: Hang with straight arms; pull the chest to the bar; lower all the way; use a band or a box jump up if needed

rows.name: Band press
rows.why: A chest press against a band anchored behind you.
rows.how: Band behind the back, ends in hand; press forward like a push up; return slowly to the chest

rows.name: Floor press
rows.why: A dumbbell or kettlebell press lying on the floor: no bench, easy on the shoulder.
rows.how: Lie on the floor with a weight in each hand; lower until the upper arms touch the floor; press up

rows.name: Step-up
rows.why: Up onto a box or stair one leg at a time: the climbing move.
rows.how: Whole foot on a box; stand up through the top leg without pushing off the back foot; step down slowly

rows.name: Single-leg calf raise
rows.why: Calf and Achilles capacity with body weight, on a step when you can.
rows.next_hard: hold a dumbbell (single-leg DB calf raise)
rows.how: Balls of the feet on a step; rise as high as you can; lower slowly until the heels drop below the step

rows.name: Pallof press
rows.why: Press a band straight out and hold against the twist: trunk control.
rows.next_hard: a stronger band, or step further out
rows.how: Band anchored to the side at chest height; press the hands straight out and resist the twist; return slowly

rows.name: Plank
rows.why: The basic front hold: trunk stiffness for every sport.
rows.next_hard: lift one foot, then one arm
rows.how: Forearms under the shoulders, body in one line; squeeze the glutes and brace; breathe and hold

rows.name: Single-leg DB calf raise
rows.why: Calf and Achilles capacity for running mileage.
rows.how: One foot on a step, dumbbell in the same hand; rise high for 3 s, pause, lower for 3 s below the step

rows.name: Slow calf drop off a step (3 s down)
rows.why: Slow lowering loads the Achilles for downhills and long runs.
rows.cautions: ankle above a twinge: both legs, no load
rows.how: Rise on both feet; shift to one foot and lower slowly for 3 to 4 s; repeat on the same side

rows.name: Seated calf raise, bent knee
rows.why: Soleus strength: most calf re-strains are in the soleus (IR-40); heavy slow raises are the tendon stimulus (TR-29).
rows.how: Sit on a bench, balls of both feet on a plate or step, dumbbells standing on your knees; rise high, pause, lower for 3 s

rows.name: Calf hold, wall lean
rows.why: Long, hard holds load the Achilles without bouncing; first-line work in a flare (IR-39, TR-29).
rows.next_hard: one leg, then hold a dumbbell
rows.how: Hands on a wall, knees a little bent, heels up high; press the balls of your feet down as hard as feels OK and hold

rows.name: Side plank
rows.why: Lateral trunk and hip control for a steady pelvis on the run.
rows.next_hard: Copenhagen plank, knee on the bench
rows.how: Elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked; lift the hips until straight; hold without letting them sag

rows.name: Suitcase carry (one heavy DB)
rows.why: Walking with one heavy weight: trunk and hip stability under load, like a pack on a climb.
rows.how: Heavy dumbbell in one hand; walk tall without leaning; switch hands each length

rows.name: Dead bug
rows.why: Front trunk control with a still low back, the position that holds the aero bars.
rows.how: On your back, arms up and knees over hips; lower the opposite arm and leg slowly while the low back stays down

rows.name: Barbell back squat
rows.why: The competition squat: the most load the legs can move, and the one lift with powerlifting norms to rank against.
rows.cautions: knee or lower back pain under load: stop
rows.how: Bar on the upper back, feet shoulder width; sit down between the heels with the chest up; stand by pushing the floor away

rows.name: Barbell bench press
rows.why: The competition press, ranked against powerlifters for anyone who already does it.
rows.cautions: shoulder pinch at the bottom: stop; use a spotter or safety arms
rows.how: Eyes under the bar, shoulder blades pinched; lower to the lower chest; press up and slightly back

rows.name: Barbell deadlift
rows.why: The competition pull from the floor, ranked against powerlifters for anyone who already does it.
rows.cautions: lower back feels uneven or rounds: stop
rows.how: Bar over the middle of the foot; grip, flat back, chest up; push the floor away and stand tall; lower with control
